messages:
marie: Heads up — since the firewall/authz cutover last night we're seeing ~40% GPU node join failures in eu-west-2 warm pool. Airgapped logs show KMS decrypt timeouts and S3 PUT 503s when trying to pull init artifacts. :grimacing:

marie: sample error:
```
2026-03-21T22:14:02Z node-evict eu-west-2: init artifact fetch failed: PUT https://s3.eu-west-2.redwood-infra/artifacts/... 503 ServiceUnavailable
2026-03-21T22:14:03Z kms decrypt error: access denied (operation timed out)
```

alex: :eyes: I see corresponding flowlog drops at the NATGW level — egress QPS spikes then RSTs. Could be the new QoS/ratecap on the egress firewall chaining into privatelink. Posting flow sample:
```
src=subnet-warmpool dst=s3.eu-west-2 proto=443 action=blocked reason=egress-ratecap qps=1200
```

devon: Is the audit exporter spamming the natgw? We had a config change to forward all keystore/audit events to the SIEM which went live with the cutover.

sam: we did increase audit sampling for keystore yesterday (for compliance) — that could easily multiply egress. Cost + QPS tradeoff was noted but maybe underestimated.

nia: options: 1) temp allowlist warm-pool subnets to bypass the ratecap (fast, blast radius low), 2) rollback audit sampling to pre-cutover (low effort), 3) raise quota with network team (longer).

marie: temp allowlist would unblock joins quickly but increases audit exposure. Need a quick rollback plan. Who can push the subnet exception? @alex?

alex: I can push a scoped allowlist for 3 subnets (warmpool-eu-1..3). Will tag with TTL 2h. Doing it now.

ops-bot: Deploy request accepted — applying firewall exception for subnets [warmpool-eu-1..3] with TTL 7200s. Change-id: fw-exc-1748909999-1

marie: confirmed — new nodes are joining again, join failures down to ~2%. Monitoring for 20m.

devon: we'll also roll back audit sampling to 10% for keystore events in eu-west-2. @sam can you coordinate? Need to capture enough for compliance but not saturate NATGW.

sam: on it. rolling back now.

nia: please create a follow-up RFC for permanent mitigations: keep audit retention, but set exporter batching + enforced backpressure, and consider private S3 endpoints or VPC endpoint for KMS to reduce egress load.

marie: Agreed. For the incident postmortem let's include cost delta from increased sampling. Early estimate: extra NAT egress ~1.3TB and ~ $180/day in eu-west-2 while it was high.

alex: change-id fw-exc-1748909999-1 reverted TTL at 2h, no further action needed. Closing here unless numbers spike. :thumbsup:

marie: thanks all :heart:
